dossiers.label: Being and becoming; the likely story
dossiers.about: Timaeus' prelude: what always is, grasped by thought with reason, and what comes to be, grasped by opinion with perception. The world has come to be, so it is an image of an eternal model; and of an image we can give only a likely account, a 'likely story'.

passage.start_quote: τί τὸ ὂν ἀεί, γένεσιν δὲ οὐκ ἔχον

parts.label: What always is, and has no becoming
parts.quote: τί τὸ ὂν ἀεί, γένεσιν δὲ οὐκ ἔχον

parts.label: The maker, the craftsman of the world
parts.quote: δημιουργὸς

parts.label: So this world must be an image of something
parts.quote: τόνδε τὸν κόσμον εἰκόνα τινὸς εἶναι

parts.label: As being is to becoming, truth is to belief
parts.quote: ὅτιπερ πρὸς γένεσιν οὐσία, τοῦτο πρὸς πίστιν ἀλήθεια

parts.label: Accept the likely story and seek nothing further
parts.quote: τὸν εἰκότα μῦθον ἀποδεχομένους

echoes.quote: καὶ ὅτι οὐσία πρὸς γένεσιν, νόησιν πρὸς δόξαν
echoes.why: The Republic's line in the same proportion: as being to becoming, intellection to opinion.

related.why: The same split of being and becoming, thought and opinion, with the same proportion.

evidence.quote: καὶ ὅτι οὐσία πρὸς γένεσιν, νόησιν πρὸς δόξαν

related.why: The prelude leads straight into why the maker made.

dossiers.label: The maker was good, and without envy
dossiers.about: Why did the maker make the world? He was good, and in the good no envy ever arises; so he wished all things to be as like himself as possible, brought order out of disorder, and made the world a living being with soul and mind.

passage.start_quote: λέγωμεν δὴ διʼ ἥντινα αἰτίαν γένεσιν καὶ τὸ πᾶν
passage.end_quote: τίνι τῶν ζῴων αὐτὸν εἰς ὁμοιότητα ὁ συνιστὰς συνέστησεν

parts.label: He was good, and the good has no envy
parts.quote: ἀγαθῷ δὲ οὐδεὶς περὶ οὐδενὸς οὐδέποτε ἐγγίγνεται φθόνος

parts.label: He wanted all to be like himself
parts.quote: πάντα ὅτι μάλιστα ἐβουλήθη γενέσθαι παραπλήσια ἑαυτῷ

parts.label: A living being with soul and mind
parts.quote: ζῷον ἔμψυχον ἔννουν

echoes.quote: φθόνος γὰρ ἔξω θείου χοροῦ ἵσταται
echoes.why: The Phaedrus: envy stands outside the divine chorus.

related.why: Next the maker composes the soul of the world.

evidence.quote: τῆς ἀμερίστου καὶ ἀεὶ κατὰ ταὐτὰ ἐχούσης οὐσίας

web.title: Plato's Timaeus
web.quote: It is the handiwork of a divine Craftsman

dossiers.label: The making of the world soul
dossiers.about: The maker mixes Being, Same and Different, then marks off portions in the double and triple series 1, 2, 4, 8 and 1, 3, 9, 27, fills the intervals with means, and fills the 4:3 intervals with 9:8 tones and a remainder of 256:243; he splits the strip in two, bends it into the circles of the Same and the Different.

passage.start_quote: τῆς ἀμερίστου καὶ ἀεὶ κατὰ ταὐτὰ ἐχούσης οὐσίας
passage.end_quote: ἐπεὶ δὲ κατὰ νοῦν τῷ συνιστάντι πᾶσα ἡ τῆς ψυχῆς σύστασις ἐγεγένητο

parts.label: Indivisible being, divisible being, and a third between

parts.label: Forcing the Different, hard to mix, into the Same

parts.label: Seven unequal circles

diagram.title: The two series of 35b–c
diagram.about: The seven portions the maker cut, set out in the shape of a Greek lambda (Λ): the doubles down one side and the triples down the other. Each number is Timaeus' own word.

The Laws: the motion of the heavens is like the circling of mind.

related.why: The cosmic circles and their harmony in the myth of Er.
The circles of the soul become the clock of time.

dossiers.label: Time, the moving image of eternity
dossiers.about: The model is an eternal living thing; no generated thing could be eternal, so the maker made 'a moving image of eternity', moving according to number: time, which came to be with the heavens; 'was' and 'will be' belong to becoming, 'is' alone to eternal being.

passage.start_quote: ὡς δὲ κινηθὲν αὐτὸ καὶ ζῶν ἐνόησεν
passage.end_quote: εἰς διορισμὸν καὶ φυλακὴν ἀριθμῶν χρόνου γέγονεν

parts.label: An image of the eternal gods, and the father rejoiced
parts.quote: ἠγάσθη τε καὶ εὐφρανθεὶς

parts.label: A moving image of eternity
parts.quote: κινητόν τινα αἰῶνος ποιῆσαι

parts.label: Eternal image moving according to number: time
parts.quote: κατʼ ἀριθμὸν ἰοῦσαν αἰώνιον εἰκόνα, τοῦτον ὃν δὴ χρόνον ὠνομάκαμεν

parts.label: Time came to be with the heaven
parts.quote: χρόνος δʼ οὖν μετʼ οὐρανοῦ γέγονεν

parts.label: Sun, moon and the planets to mark it
parts.quote: εἰς διορισμὸν καὶ φυλακὴν ἀριθμῶν χρόνου

related.why: The eternal model and its image, from the prelude.

evidence.quote: τόνδε τὸν κόσμον εἰκόνα τινὸς εἶναι

dossiers.label: The receptacle (chora)
dossiers.about: A 'third kind' besides model and copy: the receptacle and nurse of all becoming, like gold that is shaped and reshaped, a mould-stuff without features of its own; space, which is grasped by a 'bastard reasoning' and seen as in a dream.

passage.start_quote: νῦν δὲ τρίτον ἄλλο γένος ἡμῖν δηλωτέον
passage.end_quote: πρῶτον μὲν δὴ πῦρ καὶ γῆ καὶ ὕδωρ

parts.label: A third kind must now be shown
parts.quote: νῦν δὲ τρίτον ἄλλο γένος ἡμῖν δηλωτέον

parts.label: Receptacle of all becoming, like a nurse
parts.quote: πάσης εἶναι γενέσεως ὑποδοχὴν αὐτὴν οἷον τιθήνην

parts.label: The mould-stuff of everything
parts.quote: ἐκμαγεῖον

parts.label: The kind that is space, always

echoes.why: Just before: the 'wandering cause', necessity, persuaded by mind.

related.why: In the receptacle the god shapes the four kinds by forms and numbers.

dossiers.label: The elements and the regular solids
dossiers.about: The god builds fire, air, water and earth out of two right-angled triangles: pyramid, octahedron, icosahedron and cube; a fifth construction he used for the whole, 'embroidering' it. Fire is sharpest and lightest, earth the hardest to move.

passage.start_quote: πρῶτον μὲν δὴ πῦρ καὶ γῆ καὶ ὕδωρ

dossiers.label: Atlantis and ancient Athens
dossiers.about: Critias' story, from Solon, from the priests of Saïs: 'you Greeks are always children'; nine thousand years ago ancient Athens defeated the island empire of Atlantis beyond the Pillars of Heracles, which then sank in a single day and night. The Critias describes the island and breaks off.

parts.label: A strange tale, but wholly true
